_readme: Cross-language channel-wire protocol limits. The Go implementation (backend/channelwire/wire.go) and the TypeScript browser client (frontend/src/lib/reassembler.ts) frame, chunk, and reassemble the SAME encrypted channel messages, so a receiver that disagrees with the sender on any of these silently rejects or mis-splits a legitimate message rather than failing cleanly. This fixture is the single source both sides assert their constants against: a retune on one side that is not mirrored on the other reddens CI here (backend/channelwire/wire_test.go and frontend/src/lib/channel.wire-limits.test.ts) instead of drifting into a runtime interop bug. maxPlaintextPerChunk = max plaintext bytes per Noise transport message (65535 max ciphertext - 16 byte AEAD auth tag). maxMessageSize = default operator-facing application payload budget (agent line, file body). innerEnvelopeHeadroom = bytes added on top of a (configured or default) maxMessageSize for protobuf envelopes wrapping the payload; maxReassembledMessageSize = maxMessageSize + innerEnvelopeHeadroom, the receive/send-gate ceiling every receiver enforces. maxIncompleteChunked = max concurrent in-flight chunked sequences per channel before new ones are rejected. maxConfigurableMessageSize = largest max_message_size an operator may configure. pingMethod = the no-op inner RPC name both ends use for the open-time round trip that proves the E2EE session decrypts in both directions. sessionKeyMaxAgeMs = initiator in-band rekey age ceiling (channelwire.SessionKeyMaxAge). minRekeyIntervalMs = earliest age-only rekey after a successful one (channelwire.MinRekeyInterval); SoftNonceLimit bypasses. sessionKeyHardCeilingMs = absolute age past which initiators close and re-handshake (channelwire.SessionKeyHardCeiling). closeReasonTooManyConnections = the WebSocket close reason the Hub sends with a policy-violation status when a user is at max_connections_per_user; the client branches on it because every other policy-violation close means re-authenticate while this one means close a tab, so a mismatch here makes the browser give the opposite advice. closeReasonSnapshotTooLarge = the close reason the Hub sends when a subscriber's opening snapshot exceeds the entire user-events queue budget; unlike a transient shortage no retry can ever succeed, so the client must stop and surface an operator-actionable message rather than rebuilding the same snapshot forever. closeReasonForbidden = the close reason the Hub sends when an ACL check refuses the subscription; distinct from an expired credential because re-authenticating cannot grant a permission. closeReasonControlFlood = the close reason the Hub sends when a peer floods control frames past its allowance; the client must not read it as anything about the account or the credential.
